subject: Scale readiness gap analysis & action items
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex@brightbox.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: performance targets & immediate gaps

Alex — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and the items we agreed to validate before the commercial review next week. I split these into "SLO targets" (what you said you need) and "operational gaps" (what we saw in the demo and what we'll validate):

SLO targets you articulated:
- Streaming interactive API: p95 latency <= 250ms for single-user streaming (acknowledgement + first token under 120ms).
- Concurrency target: steady 300 concurrent streaming sessions with <300ms p95 for subsequent chunks.
- Throughput: bursts up to 6k simultaneous token generators across a region for scheduled batch windows (non-streaming).
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for the production inference endpoint.

Operational gaps we observed / need to validate:
1) Scale-up times: you want the platform to reach target concurrency in <60s for most burst patterns. Our initial config reached target in ~75–90s in the demo under synthetic load. Need to test with your real request distribution (short-chunk streaming + long completions).
2) Warm pool sizing: current warm pool we used was conservative (2x baseline). For your target concurrency we likely need a bank of prewarmed contexts to hit 250ms p95 consistently. We'll propose sizing options and cost tradeoffs.
3) Queueing behavior: under burst, we observed short-lived queuing that increased tail latency for 8–12s windows. We should map acceptable queue thresholds and fallback policies (smaller model, degraded streaming mode).
4) Prefix/KV priming: for streaming prompts that reuse context across sessions, priming cache hit rates matter; we flagged a 30% miss-rate in the demo workload.

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
- Alex: share a 48-hour sample of production request traces (anonymized) so we can run a replay.
- Marissa + Rishi: build a replay job and run two scenarios — steady-state concurrency ramp to 300, and a realistic burst pattern (baseline 200 -> spike 1200 over 30s).
- Kimberly: deliver a proposed warm-pool sizing matrix (SLO tradeoffs + incremental cost) and an action plan for fallback policies by EOD Friday.

Attachments: SLO-matrix-v3.xlsx (baseline vs aggressive sizing), warm-pool-diagram.png (architectural sketch).

Thanks again — I’ll start the replay setup once we have the trace.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kpark@redwood.com

From: Alex Torres <alex@brightbox.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: performance targets & immediate gaps

Kimberly — good notes, thanks. Quick clarifications from our side:
- The p95 numbers are strict for interactive user journeys (dashboard chat). For bulk async jobs we can tolerate higher latency (p95 < 1s).
- The 6k token generators number is for our daily data enrichment window and will be scheduled, so a slightly slower scale-up is acceptable there as long as it completes within 5 minutes. The critical piece is the interactive 300 conc sessions with low tail latency.

We can export a 48-hour trace but will need assistance to scrub IPs and user IDs. I’ll get ops to generate an anonymized trace and share a signed SFTP link by EOD. Also flagged one more constraint: we run across two AZs within us-west-2 and prefer not to cross-region failover during bursts.

Alex
Alex Torres
CTO (acting), BrightBox
ops@brightbox.io

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: performance targets & immediate gaps

Looping in our infra runbook. I started a ticket to prepare the replay cluster and will use two model configs:
- config-a (baseline): 1x prewarm per 100 concurrent sessions, optimistic kernel selection.
- config-b (aggressive): 3x prewarm per 100 concurrent sessions + KV cache fronting + small-model fallback at 80% queue threshold.

Planned tests:
A) Steady ramp: 0 -> 300 concurrent streaming sessions over 5 minutes, hold 10m. Measure p50/p95/p99 for first token and chunk streaming.
B) Burst spike: baseline 200 -> 1200 over 30s, maintain 60s, then decay. Inspect queue durations and warm-pool drain behavior.

Data we need from Alex: anonymized traces + typical prompt length distribution (tokens per request) + fraction of sessions that re-use context.

I’ll attach a short checklist once I spin up the replay infra. If config-b meets p95 targets at or below 250ms for streaming, we can map the incremental cost back to the BrightBox account and propose a dedicated warm pool (monthly commit).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex@brightbox.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 12:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: performance targets & immediate gaps

Alex — appreciate the quick turnaround. Two small asks to keep the replay productive: 1) include a short doc that maps anonymized trace fields to user journeys (chat vs batch) and 2) share expected percentiles for prompt token counts. We’ll start with a conservative mapping if you can’t supply the second immediately.

Tentative timeline:
- Thu 10/29: infra and replay cluster live; we run the steady ramp and capture results.
- Fri 10/30 morning: run the burst spike and validate fallback behaviors.
- Fri 10/30 EOD: deliver an internal readout (to BrightBox) with cost vs SLO tradeoffs and a recommended warm-pool commit size.

If the replay shows scale-up under 60s for your streaming-critical path we will keep the proposal in the self-serve/dedicated sizing band; if it does not, we’ll include a canary plan with stepwise capacity commitments and a contingency SLA (reduced billing rate during remediation).

Thanks — I’ll ping once the replay job is queued.

—Kimberly
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
